bull.t: Product revenue momentum and production conversion
bull.b: Strong product-led growth and conversion of design wins into mass production indicate improving commercial adoption of Sequans’ cellular IoT solutions. A growing installed program base can support recurring shipments, deepen customer relationships, and improve operating leverage as volumes scale.

bull.t: Simplified balance sheet after debt and Bitcoin exit
bull.b: Removing cryptocurrency exposure and substantially simplifying the capital structure gives management clearer financial visibility and reduces balance-sheet complexity. The resulting flexibility can support investment in core semiconductor products while making the company’s underlying operating performance easier to assess.

bull.t: Large product and RF opportunity pipeline
bull.b: A substantial multi-year product pipeline and emerging RF opportunity set broaden Sequans’ potential revenue base beyond current shipments. If programs continue moving into production, the company could diversify growth across cellular IoT, drones, defense, and other specialized connectivity markets.

bear.t: Persistent losses and operating cash burn
bear.b: Severe losses and continued cash consumption show that the current revenue base is not yet sufficient to fund operations internally. Until product scaling produces durable profitability and positive operating cash flow, Sequans remains dependent on balance-sheet resources and successful execution of its growth plan.

bear.t: Compressed margins and continuing cost pressure
bear.b: Lower gross margin reduces the earnings benefit of rising product volumes and makes the path to breakeven more dependent on cost control. Persistent component constraints could sustain pricing and input-cost pressure, limiting margin recovery even as production and customer programs expand.

The non-compliance notice creates an additional execution burden during a period when the company is already working toward profitability. Management must submit and execute a remediation plan within the cure process, while continued listing uncertainty can complicate stakeholder confidence and corporate planning.
